quote_text:
I think, uh, so what are your thoughts?
I think it’s a fair result when the  game is over. We had some parts when  
we were 1-0 up where we could’ve done  better, maybe, but also, they did well.
How the game went on…  sometimes we lost the rhythm,  
and that allowed Hearts to make their way into the  game. We gave away the ball in some situations,  
and they created momentum from that. That’s  something we need to keep working on. When  
the game is intense and we’re not fully  there, we can make small, small mistakes,  
and that can give momentum to Hearts. But  vice versa, Hearts also made some mistakes in  
certain areas, and we gained the ball. So,  it was quite a busy game in some situations.
What happened at halftime with the injury?
We need to check on him properly tomorrow. He  couldn’t keep playing, so we had to make a change.
Do you know what the injury is?
No, I want them to confirm exactly what  it is first before I say something.
Concerned for Wednesday night?
Let’s see. The good thing was that Ross  came in and did really well. He looked  
prepared. We have a good squad. Jimmy did  well, McGarry did well, Angus did well.  
A lot of players who haven’t played so much  gave a good impression on the pitch. That’s  
what we need when the games are so intense.  We need to keep everybody healthy and fresh.
Do you think the substitution  impacted the goal you conceded?
No, no, I don’t think so. These things  happen in football. It wasn’t about Jimmy,  
and the change didn’t cause that.
Was it just a lack of focus on the first action?
I don’t know exactly what happened,  but I think it was more of a hit.  
I’m not so worried about it being  a long-term issue, but let’s see.
You made six changes to the team  today. Was that to freshen things up?
Yes, we’ve had two difficult games—against  St. Mirren and Hibernian, both away. Then  
we come back down again. We needed to bring  some freshness to the team, both mentally and  
physically. That’s why we made those changes.  We have a good squad, and it’s good to see  
players who haven’t played as much doing well  on the pitch. That’s important for the future.
That’s two points dropped. Are some of the  players lacking confidence in the final third?
No, it’s not only us. It’s a competitive  league, and we’ve been playing difficult  
away games. Sometimes a draw away  from home is a good result if you  
look at how the games played  out. For example, against Hibs,  
even though we conceded in the last second for  3-2, you have to be fair and say a draw is a draw.
It might be a fair result, but of course,  you always want to win games and pick up  
points. It’s not easy. For us, it’s still a  long-term journey. We have a lot to improve,  
and that’s what we’re trying  to do every week as we grow.
You’ll probably have to up your  game on Wednesday to get a result?
Yes, and I think some parts of our game are  still really good. But during a long season,  
every team has periods where the  dynamics aren’t perfect. That’s not  
unusual—it happens. Things occur that  normally don’t, and every team faces  
this at some point. The most important thing is  how we get out of it and find the rhythm again.
Right now, during this period, we’ve had  these three away games. We’ve drawn twice  
and lost once. It’s not the perfect flow, but it  happens every year with every team. Hopefully,  
we can come out of this well and  start building momentum again.
Football is like that sometimes.

title: Jimmy Thelin FULL Post Match Press Conference | Hearts 1-1 Aberdeen
